assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned a superconducting artificial atom into a controllable quantum system coupled to a single microwave photon, opening strong-coupling, dispersive readout and quantum non-demolition measurement in a solid-state device. It is a clean case of foundational quantum optics becoming an enabling platform, and it underpins essentially all current superconducting processors. I know this field closely and judge the originality and clarity of the concept to be high.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff et al., Schoelkopf group) support a theory-plus-experiment configuration. Blais, Schoelkopf and Girvin is a coherent trio; Wallraff, who is not in the supplied credit, also made a decisive experimental contribution, so the allocation is not fully settled by the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and extended by many laboratories over two decades, with a stable interpretation. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, so this is a natural but distinct follow-on, and recognition would be timely. Some may judge the discovery too close to technology or too entangled with the 2025 award.
uncertainties: Missing Wallraff from the credited names makes the experimental credit incomplete.
Possible committee view that the 2025 award already covers the superconducting-circuit area.
As a WACQT director and a close colleague of groups in this field, I should consider recusal or conflict-of-interest limits, and my own judgment may be biased toward this field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, removed Doppler and recoil shifts for many atoms at once and brought fractional uncertainty to the 1e-18 level. This is a major advance in precision measurement, with clear discovery-level impact on tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first realised the magic-wavelength lattice clock concept; Jun Ye's group drove the strontium clock to record accuracy and many-body clock physics. Hall and Hänsch were already honoured in 2005 for frequency combs. Two laureates give a fair and well-defined allocation, though Wineland-type ion clocks and other groups overlap in the broader field.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many laboratories (JILA, RIKEN, PTB, NIST, SYRTE); the technology is mature and the physics stable. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Boundary of credit relative to ion clocks and other lattice-clock groups.
Whether the committee treats this as an instrument advance rather than a discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moiré quantum matter, a new regime of tunable correlated physics. Originality and impact are very high and the field has grown enormously.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated states and superconductivity (Cao et al.). That maps to a theory plus experiment trio. Others (Cory Dean, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Pablo's coworkers and Yuan Cao) contributed to the broader area, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have reproduced the main phenomena, but the microscopic nature of the superconducting pairing and several correlated states is still debated. The timing is plausible though perhaps a little early for the pairing mechanism.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and some correlated phases are still unsettled.
Credit allocation to experimental co-discoverers and hBN crystal growers is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised Hubbard-model physics with exquisite control, including the superfluid-to-Mott transition and quantum-gas microscopy at single-site resolution. This is a new paradigm of quantum simulation that makes basic many-body quantum phenomena visible, which I value highly.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch et al.) provided the theoretical proposal; Greiner and Bloch carried out the decisive Mott insulator experiments and microscopes; Esslinger's group demonstrated fermionic Mott states. Hänsch was a co-author of the 2002 experiment and is not in the supplied list. Selecting three from four credited names inevitably leaves out a significant contributor.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and extended; analogue quantum simulation has matured, although quantitative advantage over classical methods for open problems is still emerging. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Hard choice between Esslinger and others for the trio.
Jaksch and Hänsch contributions are not captured by the supplied credit.
Overlap with Zoller in B015 matters for combined prize choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions defined a concrete physical route to quantum computing and shaped the whole experimental field in trapped ions and neutral atoms. The originality and lasting influence are very high.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the clear theoretical originators. Experimental implementations (Wineland, Blatt, Monroe, and others) are partly recognised by the 2012 prize to Wineland and Haroche, which complicates credit but does not undermine a theory prize.
assessment.maturity: Validated by many experiments with trapped ions and neutral atoms; interpretation is stable. A theory-only prize may be seen as slightly separated from experimental recognition, but it is timely given quantum computing progress.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to reward a theory proposal after the 2012 experimental prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution links the foundations of quantum mechanics (no-cloning, Bell nonlocality) directly to information security. The BB84 protocol and Ekert's entanglement-based protocol are conceptually simple and profoundly original, with proven experimental demonstrations over fibre and satellites.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard (1984) and Ekert (1991) are the clear originators and fit a trio. The 2022 prize to Aspect, Clauser and Zeilinger covered the Bell-test foundations, so credit overlap is limited but there may be perceived duplication.
assessment.maturity: Experimental QKD is mature and field-deployed, though practical device security (side channels) is still an active issue. The physics is stable and recognition is plausible now.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as physics or computer science and cryptography.
Device security and side-channel limitations do not alter the principles but affect the practical narrative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics brought mechanical oscillators into the quantum regime, with ground-state cooling, quantum back-action and squeezing of light by motion, and links to gravitational-wave detection and transduction between microwave and optical photons. It is a clear opening of a new regime of quantum control, in a field adjacent to my own.
assessment.attribution: Vahala and Kippenberg demonstrated radiation-pressure coupling and cooling in microtoroids; Aspelmeyer drove quantum-optomechanics experiments and the review that defined the field. Other contributors such as Harris, Painter, Lehnert and Teufel overlap with credit that is not in the supplied list, so the allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across many platforms, but applications are still developing and quantum-limited achievements are more recent, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among many strong groups is unresolved.
The field may not yet have a single defining discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators and the observation in HgTe wells created a new class of quantum matter with protected edge states and strong influence across condensed matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group made the experimental observation (with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe proposal not in the supplied names). The Kane, Mele and Molenkamp trio is defensible but leaves out other significant theorists.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed in several materials, though the 2016 prize already honoured topological phases (Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz). Recognition might be seen as partly covered, but it remains mature and timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 topological phase prize.
Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's contributions are not in the supplied credit.
Condensed matter outside my own expertise, so I defer to colleagues.
